ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, M and N are points on the sides AB and AC, respectively, where AM = $ \frac{1}{4}$AB and AN = $ \frac{1}{4}$AC. What is the ratio of the area of $ \triangle AMN$ to the area of the quadrilateral MBCN?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AM = \frac{1}{4}AB$ and $AN = \frac{1}{4}AC$, and $\angle MAN = \angle BAC$,

$\therefore \triangle AMN \sim \triangle ABC$, 

$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle AMN}}{S_{\triangle ABC}} = \left(\frac{AM}{AB}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{16}$,

$\therefore S_{\triangle AMN} = \frac{1}{16}S_{\triangle ABC}$,

$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle AMN}}{S_{\text{quadrilateral }MBCN}} = \frac{S_{\triangle AMN}}{S_{\triangle ABC} - S_{\triangle AMN}} = \boxed{\frac{1}{15}}$.
